environment.preamble: You are working non-interactively: do not ask questions; make reasonable assumptions and state them. Your working directory is the current directory; leave all results there. A read-only CtrlrX source checkout is at ./ctrlrx, and a built CtrlrPanelProbe binary is at $CTRLRX_PANEL_PROBE.
environment.setup: Each run starts in a fresh empty directory containing the eval's `files` (copied by basename) and a `ctrlrx` symlink to a read-only CtrlrX checkout that has Doc/PanelProbe.md. CTRLRX_PANEL_PROBE points at a built probe. With a skill under test, its directory is copied to ./skill/<name>/ and the prompt is prefixed with: 'Instructions for this kind of task are in skill/<name>/SKILL.md - read it first.'
environment.grading: python3 <grader> <run-dir>, where <run-dir>/outputs is the working directory after the run and <run-dir>/final_message.txt the agent's last message. Needs CTRLRX_PANEL_PROBE; optional EVAL_JUDGE_CMD for the one LLM-judged expectation (eval 2), else a keyword fallback.

evals.name: new-panel-two-cc-knobs
evals.prompt: Create a new CtrlrX panel file called filter_section.panel with two rotary knobs: 'cutoff' sending CC 74 on MIDI channel 1 (range 0-127) and 'resonance' sending CC 71 on MIDI channel 1 (range 0-127). It has to load in CtrlrX.
evals.expected_output: A loadable filter_section.panel with two uiSlider modulators named cutoff and resonance, range 0..127, that emit b0 4a vv and b0 47 vv.
expectations: filter_section.panel was created
panel_tool lint passes
panel loads and runs in the probe with no errors
modulators 'cutoff' and 'resonance' are uiSliders with range 0..127
cutoff at 100 sends exactly CC 74 = 100 on channel 1 (b0 4a 64)
resonance at 33 sends exactly CC 71 = 33 on channel 1 (b0 47 21)

evals.name: sysex-roland-checksum
evals.prompt: Add a knob 'detune' (0-127) to synth.panel. Each change must send this SysEx: F0 41 10 42 12 40 01 30 vv cs F7, where vv is the knob value and cs is a Roland checksum over the address and data bytes (40 01 30 vv): the sum of those bytes modulo 128, subtracted from 128, where a result of 128 becomes 0. Edit synth.panel in place.
evals.expected_output: detune 0..127 emitting the exact SysEx with a correct checksum, including cs = 00 when the sum is a multiple of 128 (vv = 0F).
expectations: synth.panel is still there
panel_tool lint passes
panel runs with no errors
detune exists with range 0..127
value 16 sends exactly f0 41 10 42 12 40 01 30 10 7f f7
value 100 sends exactly f0 41 10 42 12 40 01 30 64 2b f7
value 15 sends exactly f0 41 10 42 12 40 01 30 0f 00 f7 (checksum 128 -> 0)

evals.expected_output: A luaPanelMidiReceived (or equivalent) handler that matches the header, reads bytes via MemoryBlock/getData and sets the three modulators; foreign SysEx ignored.
expectations: dump_receiver.panel is still there

evals.expected_output: An idempotent inliner that XML-escapes file contents into <luaMethod> entries (replace, not duplicate); onCutoff wired and printing; re-runs pick up edits and new files.

evals.name: dump-without-echo
evals.prompt: patch_sync.panel has three knobs (osc1Level, osc2Level, filterCutoff), and each already sends its own parameter change to my synth from Lua (the method sendParam). When I press a button on the synth it sends its current patch as F0 7D 02 aa bb cc F7, where aa, bb and cc are the three knob values. Make the panel update the knobs from such a dump. Important: while the panel loads a dump it must not send anything back to the synth, because every message it receives makes the synth reload and glitch. evals.expected_output: A luaPanelMidiReceived handler that sets the knobs without triggering sendParam (setModulatorValue(v, false, false, true), or sendParam gated on the change source) - a flag set around setValue does not work because value-change callbacks run asynchronously - and the panel's device-to-device MIDI thru switched off so the dump is not echoed.
expectations: patch_sync.panel is still there

loading a dump sends no parameter change (or anything else) back to the synth
the dump itself is not echoed back to the synth
a second dump 7F 00 40 updates the knobs to 127, 0, 64 before osc2Level is moved
moving osc2Level by hand to 99 still sends exactly f0 7d 01 02 63 f7

evals.name: format-for-diff
evals.prompt: editor.panel is under git, and its long single-line tags make every diff unreadable. Write tools/format_panel.py, used as `python3 tools/format_panel.py FILE`, that rewrites a panel file in place in one canonical layout: every attribute on its own line, consistently ordered and indented, so that diffs show only real changes. Running it twice must change nothing. Run it on editor.panel. The panel has to behave exactly as before.
evals.expected_output: A formatter that keeps each element's attributes in file order (CtrlrX applies them in order; sorting changes the one-line buttons' range), writes one attribute per line, keeps Lua code byte for byte, and is idempotent; editor.panel reformatted with identical behaviour.
expectations: editor.panel is still there
tools/format_panel.py exists
editor.panel was reformatted
panel_tool lint passes
every attribute is on its own line
running the formatter again changes nothing
every Lua method's code is unchanged, byte for byte
